idea: Three-tier density classification per approach from three roadside sensors (P1..P3 binary: Low 100, Medium 110, High 111) feeding a signal rule: fixed time of Q seconds per turn in normal flow, switch to a density-based interval timing in rush hour (cumulative density from sensor and camera), plus a regression tree learning the daily rush interval from history.
does: Simple actuated-signal extension: green time per phase scaled by a 3-level queue density measured from detector occupancy; rush interval learnt from the daily demand profile.
inputs: per-approach queue length or occupancy, daily profile
outputs: green time per phase per cycle
existing: partial: SCATS/SCOOT adaptive timing (planning level); actuated signals listed as not built
notes: Survey-level description only (no formula for the timing); the existing not_built list already names actuated control, so the book adds just the 3-level density rule.

idea: Context-dependent multi-objective route choice: per-vehicle fitness over travel time, congestion, fuel/emission and risk, solved by A* for distance and a genetic algorithm or Pareto trade-off otherwise; weights switch with context (high pollution -> emissions weight up; emergency -> fastest). Predictive load balancing reroutes vehicles away from forecast hotspots before they form.
does: Vehicles (or a share of them) re-plan at junctions using current road speeds with a weighted cost; EV class uses pure travel time.
inputs: live road mean speeds from Frame, cost weights per vehicle type, share of informed drivers
outputs: changed routes, reroute counts, network KPI change
existing: none (routes assigned at spawn per not_built; no dynamic rerouting mentioned)
notes: Book gives no formulas; the method is standard (dynamic user-equilibrium style re-routing as in SUMO's rerouters). Needs a test for routes remaining valid on one-way roads.

idea: Rule or autoencoder-style anomaly rule: a segment that normally flows freely whose speed suddenly drops while density rises is flagged as a possible incident; triggers dynamic rerouting.
does: Flags road segments where speed falls well below its own recent baseline while occupancy rises, and reports duration; lets the assistant detect self-inflicted blockages (stalled vehicle, over-long red) in headless runs.
inputs: per-road speed and density series from the run

idea: Rolling-horizon route guidance: each control interval T, flag link i congested or about to be if X_i(k)/C_i >= alpha (alpha in 0..1) or the forecast X_i(k+1)/C_i >= alpha; select only vehicles that will use that link and are within l hops upstream (l tuned to avoid secondary congestion on detours); compute their fastest alternative by Dijkstra on current link travel times. Dynamic routing with prediction (Alg 14.2): process arriving vehicles in random order, giving each its route from a temporary predicted state Xp(i) that already includes the earlier rerouted vehicles, so the detour does not all go the same way.
does: Periodic partial rerouting of vehicles near congested links, with sequential load update so detours are spread; compare with no rerouting via run_experiment.
inputs: per-link volume/capacity ratio (now and short forecast), alpha, hop level l, Dijkstra on current speeds
outputs: rerouted vehicle count, per-detour load, network travel time change
notes: More specific than dynamic_rerouting from Ch 6; sequential-assignment trick is the part that avoids herding. Stdlib heapq Dijkstra.

idea: Forecast link travel speed under an incident by shockwave analysis: backward-forming shockwave speed, backward recovery shockwave, queue clearance time, maximum queue length, then per-interval link state (normal, queued, recovered) and the link speed as the space/time-occupancy weighted average of states. Inputs: location, time, lanes blocked, vehicle count, duration, upstream volume, capacity at the incident.
does: Closed-form (deterministic queueing / LWR shockwave) estimate of queue length, clearance time and delay for a blocked-lane event, to sanity-check the simulation or give the assistant a fast what-if before running it.
inputs: road length, lanes blocked, upstream flow, saturation flow, incident duration
outputs: max queue (m), clearance time (s), total delay (veh-s), speeds per interval
notes: Book lists steps only, no equations; shock speeds are the standard w = (q2-q1)/(k2-k1) from the fundamental diagram. Useful validation target for blocked-lane tests.

idea: Automatic incident detection (AID) evaluated by detection rate DR, false alarm rate FAR and mean time to detect; incident timeline t0 occurs, t1 reported, t2 verified, t3 response identified, t4 arrives, t5 all lanes open, t6 response departs, t7 return to normal flow (detection, verification, response, roadway clearance, incident clearance, time to normal).
does: Scores any detector the assistant builds (e.g. incident_flag, seasonal_baseline_anomaly) against injected incidents in headless runs: DR, FAR, MTTD, plus an incident timeline table with time to return to normal flow.
inputs: injected incident log, detector alarms with times
notes: Only useful together with an incident/blockage event model in the simulation.

idea: Connected-vehicle Webster variant (CATS): C = (1.5L+5)/(1 - D/Ln) where D/Ln is cluster density relative to cluster length from connected vehicles, replacing flow ratios; plus platoon-based control as job scheduling on a processor with Oldest Job First, which beat Webster and pre-timed at low and moderate load; phase-based queue-length prediction by exhaustive enumeration / dynamic programming (Priemer and Friedrich) using vehicle position and speed.
does: Adaptive signal extension that groups approaching vehicles into platoons (gap threshold) and serves the platoon that has waited longest, with a cap on max green; compare to Webster fixed plans with run_experiment.
inputs: vehicle positions/speeds on approaches from Frame, gap threshold, min/max green
outputs: phase decision per step, delay vs Webster
existing: partial: Webster/TRANSYT/Synchro/SCATS/SCOOT planning; actuated control listed as not built
cite: Ch 14 s14.5.2 Eq 14.1-14.3 (Webster, CATS), Pandit et al. platoon scheduling
notes: Webster Eq 14.1: C=(1.5L+5)/(1-sum(v_i/s_i)/X_c); green G = C - sum(Y_i - L_i). Already in ACMS; the new part is the platoon scheduling and CV density variant. Signal-override extension hook exists.
